data.one_liner: Classes for combinatorics pseudo-lists like permutations, combinations, and subsets.
data.what_it_does: Provides memory-efficient pseudo-list classes for combinatorial structures such as permutations, combinations, compositions, amalgams, subsets, and compounds. It maps indices to selections without generating or storing all items in memory at once.
use_when: You need to work with combinations, permutations, or subsets in Dart
You are dealing with embarrassingly parallel workloads or steganography requiring indexed access to combinations
avoid_when: You need a general-purpose collection library without combinatorial math requirements
strengths: Memory efficient through index mapping instead of full list generation
Supports BigInt indices for very large combinations
Includes support for replacement and unspecified length variants
weaknesses: Niche domain-specific utility limited to combinatorics
